taobhóige tithe pobail ghleann fhinne agus leitir bric all saints day - sunday year a — november 1st 2026 thoughts on the gospel for all saints day november 1st 2026 today the church commemorates all those persons who lived in friendship with god on their earthly journey and entered through it into his glory. some saints are raised to the altars as models of virtue and love for god. but many others left an im- print of sanctity day after day that perhaps passed unnoticed to human eyes, but that never escaped the attentive and loving eyes of god. as monsignor fernando ocáriz, prelate of opus dei, said: “all saints day is the feast of that quiet and simple sanctity —sanctity without any human splendor —which seems to leave no trace in history, but shines forth before god. it leaves behind in the world a sowing of love from which nothing is lost.”for the gospel of today’s mass, the liturgy chose the passage of the beatitudes according to saint matthew. thus it underlines the fact that these are the equivalent of sanctity, both of the sanctity that makes some peo-ple famous, so to speak, and the sanctity that is only fully revealed in heaven. november novena for the dead it . you can also drop them in divers newsagents in ardara or give it to one of the committee: harry walsh, deidre ward, fr. aodhan cannon, rosemary dewhirst (glenties) or aidan mchugh. the closing date for submission is 7th november. this annual always makes a great christmas present. november prayer lord god, whose days are without end and whose mercies beyond counting, keep us mindful that life is short and the hour of death unknown. let your spirit guide our days on earth in the ways of holiness and justice, that we may serve you in union with the whole church, sure in faith, strong in hope, perfect in love. and when our earthly dwelling is ended, lead us rejoicing into your kingdom where you live for ever and ever. amen. november is the month in which we especially pray for and remember our beloved dead. the parish novena of nine masses for the deceased will take place in st connell’s church, glenties beginning on monday, 2nd november at 7:30pm mass and concluding on thursday , 12th november (excluding 7th and 8th november). mass all the faithful departed will be offered on monday 2nd november in edeninfagh at 9:30am and in fintown at 6pm. envelopes in which to write the names of our deceased will be available from the three churches at this weekend’s vigil / sunday masses. after the masses in fintown and edeninfagh, all the envelopes containing the names of our loved ones will be taken to st connell’s church for the novena masses. note re: baptisms normally take place at 2pm on saturday. in order to bring cohesion, should a family book a baptism of their child on a saturday in any particular church then all subsequent baptisms on that day will take place in the same church. to book a baptism please contact the parochial house on
